name: Can I live in my home while my kitchen is being expanded?

mainEntity.name: Can I live in my home while my kitchen is being expanded?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in your home depends on the scale of the expansion and your household's tolerance for dust and disruption. If the project involves an exterior bump-out or is partitioned off with temporary plastic barriers, you can often remain in the house by establishing a temporary cooking station in another room. However, during major structural wall removal, subfloor trenching, and long periods without running water or gas, living on-site can become inconvenient. Planning your temporary kitchen setup—such as setting up a microwave, mini-fridge, and electric kettle—is an essential preparatory step before construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many homeowners stay by setting up a temporary kitchenette, though major structural demolition and utility shutoffs create short periods of disruption.
